extracted.intended_audience: small-biotech diagnostic developers, SBIR/STTR applicants, and grant reviewers (companies developing point-of-care infectious disease tests)
extracted.subtask_description: Development, validation, regulatory clearance, manufacturing, and commercialization of a lateral flow immunoassay (LFI) diagnostic (here: Active Melioidosis Detect™) including antibody selection, analytical and field validation, GMP lot production, and 510(k) preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA 510(k) clearance as commercialization requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA clearance will provide a stamp of approval, consistency and quality; FDA clearance is critical for marketing to U.S. customers and government agencies (DoD, DTRA, DHS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical FDA submission process ranges between 3-5 years. Seek pre-submission guidance from FDA for studies required for 510(k) submission; FDA clearance will enable penetration into markets not familiar with the novel test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to FDA Quality System Regulations / Design Controls (CFR 820)
rubrics_metrics.description: The company adheres to the Quality Systems regulations of the FDA from product inception by following Design Controls mandated by CFR 820 to the validation of its equipment and processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented design controls and validation of equipment/processes are required; FDA inspections assess these systems (no 483s reported for facility).

rubrics_metrics.name: GMP manufacturing and lot production under document and design control
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce multiple lots of the LFI under document and design control and GMP for large preclinical evaluation of performance characteristics with archived patient samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalize documentation of manufacturing and quality control as well as validation of the design and process prior to large-scale production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical sensitivity (limit of detection) per sample matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Spike all available sample matrices with CPS and determine analytical sensitivity (limit of detection) in each sample matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform these experiments (Year 1) to quantify LFI detection limits in blood, urine, sputum, pus, etc., recognizing blood often has very low CFU (~1 CFU/mL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimization of LFI components for multi-matrix compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine-tune and standardize LFI prototype for compatibility with all matrices by finalizing selection of buffer, pads, membranes, blockers, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardization ensures the same prototype works across different clinical matrices (Years 1-2).

rubrics_metrics.name: In-house analytical validation following FDA pre-submission guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete in-house validation including analytical sensitivity, reactivity, specificity, cross-reactivity, reproducibility/precision, interference, and stability studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproducibility/precision studies should be performed at multiple sites (specified: 3 sites). Interference and stability studies should be included in validation plan (Years 2 & 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-site reproducibility / precision testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducibility/precision studies at 3 sites to demonstrate consistent performance across different laboratories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include inter-site variability analysis as part of preclinical validation to support regulatory submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field validation in geographic sites and comparison to gold standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate the LFI in field studies at two geographical sites using archived sera and other matrices to confirm diagnostic algorithm and compare with current gold standard diagnostic (culture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field validation should confirm real-world performance and diagnostic algorithm (Years 2 & 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevalence studies in high- and low-endemic countries
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct prevalence studies in melioidosis high and low endemic countries to assess test utility and market potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevalence data will inform market size, diagnostic algorithm, and interpretation of positive predictive value in different settings (Years 2 & 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine CPS expression profile and genetic variability impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the in vitro and in vivo expression and secretion profile of CPS and variation of CPS expression across genetic diversity of B. pseudomallei.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess antigen expression variability (Years 1 & 2) to ensure LFI antibodies detect diverse strains and to anticipate false negatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preclinical animal model evaluation (mouse and NHP aerosol model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate 4C4 AMD LFI with mouse and non-human primate aerosol models of melioidosis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animal model testing (Years 2 & 3) to assess in vivo detection and to support claims regarding antigen detectability in infection models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative ELISA (qCPS) to measure CPS in human samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify CPS in human samples with the qCPS ELISA to provide quantitative antigen data to support LFI performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use qCPS ELISA (Years 2 & 3) to correlate antigen levels with LFI signal and clinical status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce and scale-up purified antigen and lead monoclonal antibody
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale up production of purified CPS and lead candidate monoclonal antibody 4C4 (Year 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure production scale-up yields consistent quality and supply for prototype and validation lot manufacturing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide prototype tests to collaborators and develop diagnostic algorithm
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide prototype tests to collaborators for further testing of all matrices and cultures using archived specimens; develop a diagnostic algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative testing informs algorithm development and helps define intended use and performance claims (Years 1-2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reactivity and specificity assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform reactivity and specificity testing including cross-reactivity panels to ensure the assay does not detect non-target organisms or antigens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design cross-reactivity studies per pre-submission guidance and include organisms/antigens relevant to differential diagnosis (e.g., Pseudomonas spp., other endemic pathogens).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference and stability studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct interference studies (sample matrix effects, endogenous substances) and stability studies (shelf-life, storage conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stability should include room-temperature stability profiling (important for resource-poor settings) and accelerated aging tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antibody selection criteria and subclass avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Select antibodies with practical characteristics for LFI; avoid IgG3 subclass mAbs due to self-association leading to labeling difficulties and false positives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate antibody self-association via surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and prefer subclasses that label well with gold conjugates and do not self-associate at increased sample volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: LFI product characteristics for resource-poor settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Design LFI to be inexpensive, rapid, sensitive, stable at room temperature, not require expensive equipment, and accept multiple sample matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These characteristics are essential for deployment in endemic, resource-limited settings and for point-of-care use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with reader/data systems (Deki/Fionet) and data capture
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate and potentially integrate portable RDT readers (e.g., Deki Reader) that perform image analysis, determine positivity/negativity, and store clinical data in the cloud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reader compatibility with cassette formats, validate reader-driven interpretation and data transmission, and consider benefits for record keeping and remote monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory and international market certifications (ISO 13485, CE marking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain ISO 13485:2003 certification and consider CE marking to increase international marketability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISO certification facilitates international sales; CE marking permits marketing in Europe; combine with FDA clearance for broader market access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing and distribution strategy tied to regulatory status
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach distribution channels, reference laboratories, and state health labs; market as RUO in the U.S. until FDA approval and as export-use elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the U.S. FDA approval is required for routine clinical marketing; before approval consider RUO/ASR channels and targeted government contracts (e.g., Navy, DTRA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive strategy and continuous improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain competitive advantage through (a) pursuing FDA clearance and CE marking, (b) manufacturing cost-reduction strategies, (c) reinforcing alliances with distributors, and (d) using customer feedback to continuously improve product quality and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine regulatory credibility, cost control, distribution partnerships, and iterative product improvement to saturate and defend markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property protection and patent strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect innovation via patent filings (PCT application and U.S. provisional claims listed) and university/company know-how and trade secrets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document priority dates, file PCT/US and claim benefit of provisional applications; align patent strategy with commercialization timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business / revenue planning and commercial milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Forecast revenues, funding sources (contract manufacturing, product sales, federal SBIR funds), pricing expectations, and sales milestones tied to hiring and market penetration (e.g., hiring sales when sales reach $5M; estimate 10–20K tests first year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use forecasts to plan manufacturing scale-up, marketing hires, and Phase III or follow-on funding needs; consider RUO/ASR sales and government contracts as interim revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical sample availability and international clinical study cost considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that FDA clearance is hindered by limited availability of well-defined samples in the U.S.; organizing clinical studies in endemic international sites can be cost-prohibitive without strong financial support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage existing collaborators for pre-clinical and clinical studies; budget for international site studies and sample acquisition when planning Phase II/III.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of current diagnostic modalities as design constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for limitations of culture (slow), PCR (low sensitivity due to low target and inhibitors), IFA (requires fluorescence microscope), IHA (high background seropositivity), and latex agglutination (low analytical sensitivity) when defining target product profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design LFI to overcome these limitations: faster than culture, more sensitive than PCR for antigen, usable without specialized equipment, and applicable to multiple matrices.
